title: Futures dip as Nvidia's first post-Huang earnings report arrives
dek: US stock futures are modestly lower after a third straight losing day that cut the S&P 500 by nearly 2% on Monday. Nvidia reports after the close, October retail sales land at 8:30 a.m. ET, and four Fed officials speak as markets price in a December rate hike.
quick: S&P 500 futures are down about 0.3% and Dow futures about 0.4%, after Monday's 1.96% drop in the S&P 500 and 2.56% slide in the Nasdaq.
Nvidia reports after the bell, its first quarter under interim CEO Colette Kress. Analysts polled by LSEG expect revenue of about $108.9 billion.
A new Commerce Department rule requiring licenses for AI chips that could serve Chinese firms remotely hit chip stocks Monday and Asian tech overnight.
Home Depot and Disney both beat estimates this morning; Home Depot also named CFO Richard McPhail as its next CEO.
October retail sales are due at 8:30 a.m. ET. Forecasts call for a 0.1% to 0.2% rise after September's 0.8% jump.
The 10-year Treasury yield is near 5.10% and the dollar index touched a 19-month high overnight on December rate-hike bets.

blocks.head: Nvidia reports tonight, its first results since Jensen Huang resigned
blocks.what: Nvidia releases fiscal third-quarter results after the close, less than a week after founder Jensen Huang stepped down as CEO. The Wall Street Journal reports he resigned over a relationship with a woman US officials suspect was working for Chinese intelligence; CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO. Analysts expect revenue of about $108.9 billion, up roughly 91% from a year ago, according to LSEG data cited by Reuters, against company guidance of about $108 billion, with an adjusted gross margin near 74%. Reuters says the company has shed about $410 billion in market value since the resignation, and the stock edged lower again pre-market.
blocks.why: Nvidia is the largest weight in the S&P 500 and the bellwether for AI spending, so its outlook will drive chipmakers, cloud and data-center suppliers, utilities tied to power demand, and the Nasdaq broadly. Previews from several outlets say guidance for next quarter, China exposure, and any leadership or governance update will matter more than the third-quarter numbers themselves.
blocks.watch: Fourth-quarter revenue and margin guidance, commentary on the new export rule, and whether the board says anything about the CEO search. The WSJ and CNBC report the board is not considering reinstating Huang, despite a public campaign by some tech figures.

blocks.head: US tightens rules on China's remote access to AI chips
blocks.what: The Commerce Department issued an interim rule on Monday requiring a license to ship advanced AI chips to any data center worldwide that gives companies headquartered in China, Macau or other arms-embargoed countries access to large amounts of computing power, according to TechCrunch and Bloomberg. Shipments to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil also now need a license, with a carve-out for US-headquartered companies. Existing operators get 90 days to obtain licenses. Separately, the Commerce and Justice departments said they have been investigating Nvidia partner Megaspeed since 2024.
blocks.why: The rule cuts into a fast-growing business of renting AI computing to Chinese firms through third countries. Nvidia fell more than 4% Monday and the Philadelphia semiconductor index dropped as much as 5.5% intraday, per Bloomberg; the selling spread to Asian and European chip stocks overnight.
blocks.watch: How Nvidia quantifies the impact tonight, and any response from Beijing as President Trump heads to meetings with Xi Jinping this week.

blocks.head: Markets price a December Fed hike; four officials speak today
blocks.what: Rate-futures markets now lean heavily toward a quarter-point hike at the Fed's December 9 decision after hot October inflation and a strong jobs report. Recent estimates of the odds range from about 80%, per ING, to near certainty, per CME FedWatch figures cited late last week. Governor Christopher Waller has said a half-point move could be warranted if core inflation keeps running at 0.3% a month or more, according to Newsquawk. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh on Monday focused on AI's economic effects and gave no hint on rates, the WSJ reported.
blocks.why: Higher rate expectations have pushed the 10-year yield above 5%, lifted the dollar and pressured gold, crypto and richly valued growth stocks. Any talk of a half-point hike today would likely push short-term yields and the dollar higher.
blocks.watch: Waller at 9:10 a.m. ET is the key speaker; Musalem, Hammack and Williams also appear. FOMC minutes come Wednesday afternoon.

blocks.head: Retail sales and Home Depot give a read on the consumer
blocks.what: October retail sales are due at 8:30 a.m. ET. Economists polled by Reuters expect a 0.2% rise after September's 0.8% gain; the consensus in the calendar below shows 0.1%, with sales excluding autos seen up 0.4%. Before the open, Home Depot reported adjusted earnings of $3.86 a share on revenue of $43.4 billion, up 4.9%, both ahead of estimates, with comparable sales up 2.2%. It now expects adjusted EPS to grow about 2% this year and named CFO Richard McPhail as its next CEO, per CNBC; shares slipped about 1% pre-market.
blocks.why: A firm spending number would reinforce the case for a Fed hike and could push yields up; a weak one could ease rate pressure but raise growth worries. Retailers and consumer discretionary stocks are most exposed. Home Depot's report showed fewer transactions but higher average spending, which analysts link to high mortgage rates holding back housing activity.
blocks.watch: Industrial production at 9:15 a.m. and the NAHB homebuilder index at 10 a.m.

blocks.head: Disney beats estimates, raises dividend by a third
blocks.what: Disney reported fiscal fourth-quarter revenue up 16% to about $25.9 billion and adjusted EPS of $1.77, above the $1.67 analysts expected, according to the company's filing and Zacks. The quarter included an extra week, which Disney estimated added about 17 cents to full-year adjusted EPS. It raised its dividend 33%, targeted $3 billion in annual cost savings by fiscal 2029, and guided to double-digit adjusted EPS growth in fiscal 2027.
blocks.why: Disney is a large holding in communication services, one of Monday's weakest sectors. Streaming revenue rose 19% and parks income grew 20%, a read-through for media and travel spending.

blocks.head: Geopolitics: Hormuz attacks, Kerch Bridge, Trump's Asia trip
blocks.what: CNBC reports Iran escalated threats as a third US aircraft carrier arrived in the Middle East, and at least one tanker was struck in the Strait of Hormuz over the weekend. Ukraine damaged the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, forcing it to close, according to the NYT, BBC and Guardian. President Trump began a 48-hour Asia trip in the Philippines and is scheduled to meet Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, the NYT reports.
blocks.why: So far oil has looked past the Hormuz incidents: Brent fell 3.6% Monday as Middle East exports recover. Any sign of a trade deal or new friction at the Xi meeting could move chip stocks, the yuan and Asian markets.

blocks.text: Asia

Asian markets fell for a second day as the US chip rule and Nvidia's turmoil weighed on technology names. Japan's Nikkei 225 dropped 1.3% and Hong Kong's Hang Seng lost 1.0%, while the Shanghai Composite slipped 0.5%. Chip-heavy South Korea and Taiwan saw bigger losses, according to regional market reports, with Samsung Electronics, SoftBank and Kioxia among the decliners. Japan's economy is also on investors' minds after data on Monday showed an unexpected third-quarter contraction, which CNBC tied to higher energy costs after household subsidies expired.
Europe

European stocks are lower across the board: the Stoxx 600 is down about 0.7%, Germany's DAX 0.8% and London's FTSE 100 0.7%. Chip-equipment makers such as ASML fell on the US export rule, according to market reports. Deutsche Bank shares dropped after a group of media outlets published stories based on about 15 million leaked documents alleging control failures, including ties to Russian clients; MarketWatch said as much as 3.8 billion euros of its market value was erased at one point. Germany's ZEW sentiment survey and the European Commission's autumn forecasts are due today.
Currencies

The dollar index is little changed near 103.6 after touching a 19-month high around 103.7 overnight, according to FXStreet and other reports, as December hike bets widen the gap between US and overseas rates. The euro is at about $1.099, near its lowest since spring 2025. The yen is around 159 per dollar, just shy of the 160 level traders watch for possible Japanese intervention. The pound is steady near $1.319, and China's yuan is little changed around 6.67 per dollar.

As of the latest data, S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 futures are each down about 0.3% and Dow futures about 0.4%, a smaller decline than Monday's cash session. On Monday the S&P 500 fell 1.96% to 7,416.59, its third straight loss and, per Reuters, its biggest three-day drop since June. The Nasdaq Composite lost 2.56% and the Russell 2000 1.73%. The VIX fear gauge rose to about 23.5, a level that signals elevated but not extreme stress.

The tone is cautious rather than panicked: traders appear to be waiting for retail sales, Waller's remarks and, above all, Nvidia tonight. Treasury yields are slightly lower this morning, offering a little relief to stocks, while the dollar holds near its highs.

Treasury yields are edging lower for a second day as investors seek safety from the tech selloff. The 2-year is near 4.79%, down about 3 basis points; the 10-year is near 5.10%, down about 2; and the 30-year is near 5.45%. The 10-year moved back above 5% last Thursday after hot inflation data. The curve slopes upward: the 10-year yields about 31 basis points more than the 2-year, meaning investors want extra pay to hold longer-term debt amid inflation and heavy government borrowing.

Fed officials have signaled a willingness to raise rates further. Waller has said he would back at least a quarter-point hike in December and possibly a half point if core inflation stays hot. Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack has said she prefers smaller, steady increases. St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem called for more hikes in late October. Chair Warsh avoided rate signals on Monday. ING says markets imply about 90 basis points of tightening over the next 12 months.
Fed speakers today (ET)

items: 7:30 a.m.: St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem
9:30 a.m.: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack
2:25 p.m.: New York Fed President John Williams

blocks.text: Monday was a broad defensive rotation. Technology was the worst S&P 500 sector, down 3.4%, as Nvidia and other chipmakers fell on the export rule and leadership worries. Energy lost 2.0% as oil dropped, and industrials (-1.9%), communication services (-1.8%) and consumer discretionary (-1.5%) also lagged. Only consumer staples (+0.3%) and utilities (+0.2%) rose. Financials fell 0.9%, with banks also hit by reports of app outages at several large banks; JPMorgan blamed a software bug and said it was not cyber-related, according to CNBC.
Pre-market movers

items: Nvidia: slightly lower ahead of tonight's results after a roughly 4% drop Monday.
Home Depot: down about 1% despite beating estimates, after naming CFO Richard McPhail as CEO effective November 23.
Disney: in focus after beating revenue and profit estimates and raising its dividend 33%.
JD.com: in focus after reporting third-quarter revenue up 3.5% to 309.6 billion yuan, according to its filing; reports differ on how results compared with estimates.

blocks.text: Oil

WTI crude is near $85.65 a barrel and Brent near $92.36, both roughly flat after Brent fell 3.6% Monday. Reuters says Brent is down about 22% this month as Middle East exports recover and the International Energy Agency expects a supply surplus this quarter. Attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and a third US carrier in the region have kept a risk premium in place but have not reversed the decline. Weekly inventory data from the API come this afternoon.
Gold

Gold is near $3,858 an ounce, up slightly today but held below $3,900, which the WSJ attributes to expectations of a December Fed hike. Higher yields and a strong dollar raise the cost of holding a metal that pays no interest.
Crypto

Bitcoin is near $64,150, down about 1.3% over the past day, and Ether near $1,790, down about 1.6%. CNBC reported Bitcoin briefly slid to around $62,000 on Monday as a wave of forced selling by leveraged traders hit, and the WSJ says both coins are hovering near multi-month lows as appetite for risk fades.

items: 8:30 a.m. ET, retail sales (October): the day's main release. Forecasts call for 0.1% to 0.2% growth after 0.8%; core sales seen up 0.4% after 0.9%.
8:30 a.m., import prices: expected up 0.7%, a check on imported inflation and tariff pass-through.
9:15 a.m., industrial production: expected flat after a 0.7% gain; capacity use about 76.8%.
10:00 a.m., NAHB homebuilder index: expected to stay at 29, a weak level reflecting high mortgage rates.
Fed speakers throughout the day, with Waller most closely watched.

rows: Revenue vs. about $108.9B consensus; fourth-quarter guidance; gross margin near 74%; impact of new China export rule; CEO search.
Beat with $3.86 adjusted EPS and $43.4B revenue; new CEO; full-year EPS growth outlook of about 2%.
Beat with $1.77 adjusted EPS; 33% dividend hike; fiscal 2027 double-digit EPS growth target; extra-week boost.
Revenue up 3.5% to 309.6B yuan; margins improved from a year ago; read on Chinese consumer demand.

blocks.text: After Nvidia tonight, the focus shifts to the Fed and the AI trade. Wednesday brings housing starts and the minutes of the Fed's last meeting at 2 p.m. ET, which could show how many officials favor faster hikes. Anthropic is expected to price its IPO Wednesday and start trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT on Thursday, according to CNBC and Bloomberg, at a range of $70 to $78 a share, a test of investor appetite for AI. Thursday has weekly jobless claims and the Philadelphia Fed factory survey, plus the release of the video game GTA VI. Friday ends with the University of Michigan's final consumer sentiment and inflation-expectations readings. More than a dozen Fed speeches are scheduled through Friday, including Waller again and Governor Lisa Cook.

bottom_line: Markets are steadier but defensive after three losing days, with chip stocks under pressure from the new export rule and rates held up by expected Fed hikes. Nvidia's results tonight are the main event for the rest of the week.
